tasks.task: List sponsor assets, value them and package tiers

items.when: Before pitching anyone, to list every asset with a real audience number and package a few tiers
When the inventory, the prices and the tiers must be worked through and written up together
When the client is a charity or club event, to get a second set of tiers and benefits to compare
When you want three tiers drafted from costs, with a reason the middle one should win
When the tiers are drafted, to run them as a sponsor would: cost, audience fit and what a trial looks like
When the package is logo placement only and a sponsor will compare it on price alone
When the tiers are set and the deck must carry audience, packages, proof and the ask
Before the slides, to outline how belief builds and where the sponsor is asked to decide
When the deck has no look yet, to compare three slide directions made at real size
When the client needs a real PowerPoint file they can edit for each sponsor
When the deck is drafted, to check slide count, talk time and type size
Before it goes out, to read the deck as a marketing manager who gets ten of these a week
When the deck is about the event and never about what changes for the sponsor

tasks.task: Build the audience numbers a sponsor can trust

items.when: When each asset needs a number from the client's own counts, not a guess
When there is survey or sign-up data and you need a profile of who the audience is
When no audience data exists and a short survey must be planned with a fair sample
When you have past sponsor results and quotes and must pick which to show and where
Before any number goes in a deck, so it has a source, a date and a method

tasks.task: Score and rank a sponsor prospect list

items.when: When you have a list of businesses you know and want who to call first, with reasons
When scoring should lead straight into ranked calls and tailored pitches
When you want a second ranking by fit and recent contact to compare with your scores
When the client's own contact list is short and needs more companies that fit
When a top prospect needs a sourced file on what it sponsors now and who decides
When you need to see which brands sponsor similar events or shows, with links

tasks.task: Write the pitch email, follow-ups and forwardable note

items.when: For each top prospect, to get a short tailored pitch, two follow-ups and a note they can forward
Before writing, to compare three plans for the pitch and its follow-ups
When the pitch should sound like the founder and tie to something specific about the company
When a prospect is quiet and each follow-up needs a new reason and a stop rule
When the first replies are no, to rework the pitch from each objection
Before sending, to test what the pitch claims and tighten it

tasks.task: Write a proposal for one sponsor

items.when: When a prospect says send me something and needs two pages built around their goals
When the proposal follows a scored list and a pitch and should carry the same reasons
When the sponsor could take one big asset or many small ones, to show both with money and dates
When you start from a call with the sponsor and want follow-up, costing and dates in order
Before sending, to read it as the sponsor and list what they would still have to ask

tasks.task: Prepare a sponsor meeting and the questions to ask

items.when: Before a first meeting, to get a brief on the person, a plan and a note to send after
When you need the questions that find what the sponsor wants to achieve and how they measure it
When sponsors raise the same doubts, such as reach or proof, and you need an answer for each
When the meeting plan leans on pressure instead of real proof and honest limits
When a sponsor asks for a lower price and you need an opening, questions and a fallback
When the sponsor is a big brand and the client is a small club or show
When you must refuse a demand such as category exclusivity for free and keep the relationship
When the client is ready to drop the price before asking what the sponsor needs

tasks.task: Draft the deliverables schedule, agreement and invoice

items.when: When the deliverables schedule should be lifted from the proposal for the contract
When a simple agreement is needed for a lawyer to check
When the sponsor sends their own contract, to rate the clauses that could hurt the client
When the deal is signed and the first payment needs an invoice with checked totals

tasks.task: Set up and run the sponsor fulfilment tracker

items.when: When a sponsor signs and every promise needs a due date, an owner and proof
When you want the steps from signed contract to renewal ask in order
When promises were also made on calls and emails and must be added to the register
When open actions sit across meeting notes and threads and need one list with owners
At the end, to check each deliverable against proof it was delivered and accepted

tasks.task: Check sponsored content labels and sponsor claims

items.when: Before a paid read, video, post or newsletter slot goes out, to check the label and its place
When the sponsor's copy may break a platform's ad rules, to flag risky lines
When the sponsor's message makes claims, to see which are backed and which go too far
When you are unsure which advertising rules apply in the countries the audience is in

tasks.task: Write the sponsor's read, post or newsletter slot

items.when: When the sponsor wants ideas for the placement, to get nine or more and the best ones made
When the slot should rest on one real fact about the sponsor, with a source for every line
When the slot is a block in a newsletter and needs copy by section
Before it runs, to check the ad label and the sponsor's claims

tasks.task: Write the season wrap-up report for a sponsor

items.when: At the end of a season or event, to show every promise with its proof before the renewal ask
When you have reach and click numbers and need trends, wins and misses written up
When you want a second one-page opening with the result and numbers first, to compare
When a good result should also become a short case study for next season's deck
Before the report goes, so each number traces to a screenshot, export or count

tasks.task: Plan the renewal ask and keep sponsors warm

items.when: When the wrap report is done and the renewal conversation needs its timing and offer
When there are several sponsors and you want renewals due in 90 days flagged with a call plan
When a sponsor should get a thank-you with one specific, true appreciation and no ask
When next season's rate is higher and the sponsor needs a letter that explains why
When the renewal will take several messages, to compare three ways to pace them
Before the renewal email goes, to cut it and check it asks for one thing
When the sponsor only hears from the client when money is due
When there is a date by which sponsors must be signed and the weeks before it need planning
When the season could chase one headline sponsor or many small ones, to compare both
When calls keep slipping and the week needs a protected block and a reason to call each lead
Each week of the season, to see what moved and which sponsors to act on today

tasks.task: Plan sponsor activations and the launch announcement

items.when: When the sponsor wants more than a logo, to get joint campaign ideas and a plan
When the partnership is announced and both sides must say the same thing
When the activation is at an event and needs a plan to draw people and follow up
When the activation is a banner and the sponsor has no real part in what the audience does

tasks.task: Plan sponsorship income for a charity or club

items.when: When a charity or club needs its assets listed and tiers that fit local businesses
When the event, audience and benefits are known and you need tiers, pitch copy and a promise list
When sponsorship is one income line in an event budget with other income to plan
When the board asks if sponsorship income is worth the risk and effort

always.when: Before any audience number or result reaches a sponsor, so it has a dated source
Before a deck, proposal or report goes, to catch typos and a sponsor name spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the sponsorship deck or wrap report must be laid out to a finished standard
When sponsor promises depend on the event plan: stands, signage, stage time and run sheet
When a charity's sponsorship sits beside grants and donor appeals in one income plan
When sponsor reads must be scripted, recorded and placed in episodes
When ad labelling or charity tax treatment needs a firm answer
When the prospect list is long and needs research and outreach at volume

gaps: No library item lists the sponsorable assets of an event, club, podcast or newsletter and values each one
No library item prices podcast reads or newsletter slots from downloads and open numbers
No library item builds a media kit or an audience numbers page with a method note
No library item writes a sponsorship deck; only general pitch and slide items exist
No library item scores local businesses as sponsor prospects on fit, signs of budget and warmth
No library item checks sponsored content labels against UK, US and EU rules by platform
No library item writes a sponsorship agreement's deliverables schedule or weighs an exclusivity clause
No library item builds a sponsor fulfilment tracker with proof such as screenshots and photos
No library item writes an end-of-season sponsor report that pairs each promise with its proof
No library item covers charity tax lines between sponsorship and advertising income
No library item writes a host-read sponsor script for a podcast
No library item gives sponsor activation ideas for events, clubs or shows
